verdict.rationale: three.js ships versioned releases (npm reports 0.186.0) with per-release changelogs and an official wiki Migration Guide that has version-to-version sections such as 185→186, so breaking changes are documented at each upgrade. However, the evidence never shows a formal deprecation policy (timelines, warning periods, or stability guarantees). The 0.x versioning and the llms.txt advice to 'always use latest version' point to a rolling-change model rather than stable versioned APIs. Missing for 10: an explicit documented deprecation policy, stability or semver guarantees, and independent corroboration of how upgrades go in practice.
